LESSON: READING 5.2.1 SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use antonyms and synonyms?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use synonyms and antonyms in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication.  Use reference materials such as the encyclopaedia and the dictionary to locate synonyms and antonyms. Learners who may not turn pages to use page- turners or be supported by peers. They could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to record findings.  Check the meaning and pronunciation of synonyms and antonyms from the dictionary  Search for synonyms and antonyms from print and digital Why do we use antonyms and synonyms? 42 texts. Control light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light while using digital devices.  Create a crossword puzzle using synonyms and antonyms and share it online.  Use synonyms and antonyms in sentences  Match words with their antonyms from a list of words,  Practise pronouncing synonyms and antonyms in pairs. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views.  Design and display a chart with antonyms and synonyms of words correctly spelled.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital Literacy is developed as the learner interacts with digital devices and uses them to access online encyclopedia and

dictionary

 Learning to learn is enhanced as learners work independently when looking up the meanings of words in the dictionary and

encyclopedia.

43

Values:
Patriotism is enhanced as the learner gains a sense of belonging to the family while constructing sentences using

synonyms and antonyms about family.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of synonyms and antonyms to their learning of vocabulary in Kiswahili.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

Social cohesion is enhanced as learners construct sentences on varied issues such as family set- up using synonyms and

antonyms of words.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts,
2. spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency,
3. use synonyms and antonyms in sentences,
4. appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication.  Use reference materials such as the encyclopaedia and the dictionary to locate synonyms and antonyms. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views.  Design and display a chart with antonyms and synonyms of words correctly spelled.
